items.followUp: Derive the second equation of motion using a velocity-time graph.

rubric.why: The graph represents speed changing from u to v during time t.
rubric.description: Shows or describes a correctly labelled speed-time graph.
rubric.how: Award for a graph or description with speed and time axes and the initial and final speeds labelled.

rubric.why: The slope of a speed-time graph is change in speed divided by time.
rubric.description: Expresses the slope of the graph.

rubric.why: For uniform acceleration, the slope is acceleration.
rubric.description: Relates the graph's slope to acceleration.

rubric.why: Rearranging the acceleration relation gives the first equation of motion.
rubric.description: Obtains the first equation of motion.

modelAnswer: Draw a speed-time graph with time t on the horizontal axis; speed changes from u at t = 0 to v at time t.
Slope of the speed-time graph = change in speed ÷ time = (v − u)/t.
For uniform acceleration, slope = a, so a = (v − u)/t.
Hence, v = u + at, the first equation of motion.

items.followUp: A 2 kg ball is thrown vertically upwards at 10 m s⁻¹. Find its maximum potential energy and its kinetic energy just before it returns to the ground. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: The mass must be converted to kilograms and the given velocity and gravitational acceleration recorded in SI units.
rubric.description: Records the given data in SI units.
rubric.how: Award for m = 0.5 kg, u = 15 m s⁻¹ and g = 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: At maximum height the velocity is zero; using the vertical motion relation gives h = 11.25 m for g = 10 m s⁻².
rubric.how: Award for a correct maximum-height calculation and result.

rubric.why: The potential energy at maximum height is mgh.
Neglecting air resistance, mechanical energy is conserved and the stone regains its initial kinetic energy at ground level.
rubric.description: Uses conservation of mechanical energy for the return to the ground.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the kinetic energy on impact equals the initial kinetic energy, assuming negligible air resistance.

rubric.why: The initial kinetic energy, and hence the kinetic energy on hitting the ground, is 56.25 J.
rubric.description: Calculates the kinetic energy when the stone hits the ground.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 500 g = 0.5 kg, u = 15 m s⁻¹, g = 10 m s⁻².
At maximum height, v = 0; use v² = u² − 2gh.
(ii) Neglecting air resistance, the stone regains its initial kinetic energy when it hits the ground.

items.followUp: What is the least count of a micrometer screw gauge, and how is it determined?

rubric.why: Least count is the smallest length an instrument can measure accurately.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is the smallest length measurable accurately with the instrument.

accept: value of one main scale division
rubric.why: For vernier callipers, the least count is determined from the relationship between one main-scale division and one vernier-scale division.
rubric.description: Explains how the least count is determined.
rubric.how: Award for stating L.C. = 1 MSD − 1 VSD, or an equivalent method of determining that difference.

modelAnswer: The least count of vernier callipers is the smallest length that can be measured accurately with them.
It is measured by finding the difference between one main-scale division and one vernier-scale division: L.C. = 1 MSD − 1 VSD.
